review_corrections.finding: amplitude calibration uncertainty not propagated; p quoted to 4 digits
review_corrections.change: amplitude nuisance sigma_r = hypot(jk4-trace scatter / excess, calibration SE / excess); per-mock truncated-normal amplitude draws give the marginal p; fixed 16%/84% amplitude ensembles give the band

review_corrections.finding: DIFF families not jointly calibrated; they are empirical differential-selection fields, not LSS
review_corrections.change: single-selection jackknife trace of the DIFF families measured against its data target in fresh mocks

scope: Null mocks are Cox processes with positions independent of the flux pair; the common dipole cancels in the contrast by construction. Clustering amplitudes are fitted to the data's own NSIDE=4 delete-one jackknife traces (one sky); the angular shape of each field is assumed, not fitted. The DIFF families are empirical differential-selection (excess-variance) fields on the resolved/migrating classes, not large-scale structure, and are not jointly calibrated (their single-selection jackknife trace exceeds the data target). Their C_1 is the power law extrapolated to l=1; the NSIDE=4/8 jackknife traces and the NSIDE8/4 ratio are insensitive to the transverse l=1 mode, which lies inside the fitted log-linear model, while that mode sets most of the null contrast covariance. Every p_mc is therefore conditional on an assumed C_1 (a random resolved-fraction dipole of per-component RMS sqrt(3 C_1/4pi)); no family's p_mc is the LSS/selection-null p-value, and C_1 = 0 is not a conservative limit. The mocks do not model source multiplicity, spatially varying flux calibration or a physical redshift-dependent bias, and they under-predict the data's per-selection pixel overdispersion. No physical Pi or Bianchi inference is made.
